body: Can you paste in the console output when this happens?

```
$ eslint -v
v0.14.1

$ eslint blah.js

fs.js:695
  return binding.stat(pathModule._makeLong(path));
                 ^
Error: ENOENT, no such file or directory 'c:\Users\Ilya\Documents\github\eslint\blah.js'
    at Object.fs.statSync (fs.js:695:18)
    at walk (c:\Users\Ilya\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\eslint\lib\util\traverse.js:36:15)
    at c:\Users\Ilya\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\eslint\lib\util\traverse.js:102:9
    at Array.forEach (native)
    at traverse (c:\Users\Ilya\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\eslint\lib\util\traverse.js:101:11)
    at CLIEngine.executeOnFiles (c:\Users\Ilya\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\eslint\lib\cli-engine.js:269:9)
    at Object.cli.execute (c:\Users\Ilya\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\eslint\lib\cli.js:178:65)
    at Object.<anonymous> (c:\Users\Ilya\AppData\Roaming\npm\node_modules\eslint\bin\eslint.js:13:20)
    at Module._compile (module.js:456:26)
    at Object.Module._extensions..js (module.js:474:10)
```

This is the expected behavior. In #1296 we discussed this and agreed that it should throw before linting.

But you are right, that the code wasn’t cleaned up completely, the `else` branch wasn’t removed. Seems like there was no test for this branch, because no test was failing.

I don’t agree that we should revert to the old behavior. The old behavior doesn’t prevent linting of other files.
Let's just remove the `else` then and maybe add a comment to say an error will be thrown when a for doesn't exist?

**What is the purpose of this pull request? (put an "X" next to item)**

[X] Bug fix ([template](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/eslint/eslint/master/templates/bug-report.md))

See #7390 for the template.

**What changes did you make? (Give an overview)**

Since #1296 and #1831, ESLint should throw errors if the given file did not be found. But ESLint does nothing (then exits with zero) since v1.4.0 due to the glob pattern support. I think this is unintentional because we seemed to do no discussion about the behavior that patterns matches no file.

ESLint shows nothing if target files have no problem, too. So the users cannot distinguish between no problem and typo from the result. I think it's not good.

This PR changes the behavior about patterns which match no file.
~~It judges for each pattern, then it generates an error message "File Not Found" for the file if the pattern matches no file.~~ If there are one or more patterns which match no file, ESLint will throw a fatal error.

<details><summary>

~~**For Examples:**~~</summary>



Those are old.

```
$ eslint non-exist.js

non-exist.js
  1:1  error  File Not Found

✖ 1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)
```

```

  1:1  error  File Not Found

✖ 1 problem (1 error, 0 warnings)
```

```

C:\Users\t-nagashima.AD\Documents\GitHub\eslint\test.js
  0:0  warning  File ignored because of a matching ignore pattern. Use "--no-ignore" to override

non-exist/**/*.js
  1:1  error  File Not Found

✖ 2 problems (1 error, 1 warning)
```

```
$ eslint test.js non-exist/**/*.js --no-ignore

C:\Users\t-nagashima.AD\Documents\GitHub\eslint\test.js
  2:1  error  Use the global form of 'use strict'  strict
  2:1  error  Unexpected console statement         no-console

non-exist/**/*.js
  1:1  error  File Not Found

✖ 3 problems (3 errors, 0 warnings)
```

</details>

<details><summary>

**For Examples:**</summary>



```
$ eslint non-exist.js

Oops! Something went wrong! :(

The given pattern "non-exist.js" was not found.
Please check for typing mistakes in the pattern.
```

```

```

</details>

**Is there anything you'd like reviewers to focus on?**
- Is the direction of this PR good?
- We have a long time since v1.4.0. Though this PR is a bug fix which increases errors, maybe we should mark this PR as breaking.
